daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo is scheduled to attend PAN's 28th anniversary celebration at JCC Senayan tonight, as the party's chairman Zulhas explained his reasons for remaining loyal to the president in coalition. Energy Minister Bahlil responded to discussions about raising the parliamentary threshold to 5 percent, while Gerindra opened the possibility of coalition with PDI-P for the 2029 presidential election. The president also recounted complaining to Jokowi about a minister who refused to meet with him.

  • President Prabowo gave directives to the National Energy Council on fuel availability, E50 preparation, and the Oil and Gas Bill, while Energy Minister Bahlil warned that subsidized fuel should not be used by wealthy citizens driving BMWs.
  • The Home Affairs Ministry awarded honors to local governments in Maluku and Nusa Tenggara for their performance, with North Maluku receiving Rp 9 billion in prize money.
  • Minister Tito announced that President Prabowo added Rp 20 billion in emergency spending allocation for East Nusa Tenggara.
  • The DPR called for halting ship operations that do not meet standard operating procedures following the KM Virgo Transport 8 accident.
  • President Prabowo stated that the entire education system must be reformed starting with teacher recruitment.
  • The Attorney General's Office revealed flows of fees from expedited special haj pilgrimage funds to cars and houses of officials during Yaqut's era, with prosecutors expressing surprise at a special staffer's confession of borrowing half a billion rupiah.
  • A DPRD Jakarta member named Bebizie failed to appear for KPK questioning.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia is preparing to welcome the arrival of Giuseppe Garibaldi, Indonesia's prospective first aircraft carrier, with the Defence Minister set to receive the vessel as it entered Indonesian waters ahead of its Jakarta arrival. Defence Minister Sjafrie met with Chinese generals in Beijing, stating that Indonesia remains open to all countries, while senior minister Luhut met China's Foreign Minister saying Indonesia wants to emulate China's development approach.

  • Vice President Gibran urged stronger protection for Indonesian migrant workers in Malaysia.
  • Indonesian peacekeepers received UN recognition in the Central African Republic.
  • Indonesia stated it adheres to ASEAN protocols amid transboundary haze issues.
  • Vice President Gibran called for faster establishment of an ASEAN Halal Council.
  • The Foreign Ministry spokesperson acknowledged receiving a message from an Indonesian citizen allegedly serving as a Russian soldier, with the individual sending messages to the Foreign Minister through a spokesperson.

Other

The Food and Drug Monitoring Agency (BPOM) deployed two deputies to investigate a "cadaver skin" skin booster product, as food poisoning incidents continue with 37 students in Kediri receiving treatment after suspected food poisoning from street food (MBG). BPOM received Rp 1.93 trillion for 2027 budget, with Rp 509 billion allocated to monitor street food vendors. The Attorney General's Office revealed state losses in the KSO PT Pertamina EP case reached Rp 2 trillion.

  • Basarnas ended the 10-day search for five journalists and three crew members missing in the Sunda Strait, with ANTARA mourning its missing photojournalist, though no leakage was confirmed from the KM Virgo wreckage.
  • Energy Minister Bahlil announced that a new oil and gas body will report directly to President Prabowo, following an energy council meeting on fuel and oil strategy.
  • A Vietnamese ride-hailing service has begun operating in Jakarta.
  • Indonesia announced that imports will continue smoothly ahead of October's halal certification mandate.
  • Amnesty International highlighted the deaths of 94 people at East Nusa Tenggara earthquake evacuation sites.
